next_step: Schedule 2-day on-site dedicated-capacity sizing workshop; run baseline load tests and token/sec profiling
notes:
Summary: Large healthtech platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for patient-facing chat assistants and embeddings-based clinical search. Primary ask: predictable throughput + strict latency SLOs for production. They want a hands-on sizing workshop to convert observed traffic into reserved GPU commitments and SLA terms.

Context / Qs from AE/SE: 
- Current infra: hybrid (GCP us-east + private datacenter for PHI). Want VPC peering and optional air-gapped on-prem for certain workloads.
- Use mix: chat assistants (multi-turn), embeddings for search across records, and high-volume reranking for triage.
- Model preference: Llama-3-Chat-13B quantized int8 on Dedicated; fallback to Llama-3-7B for overflow and lower-cost routing.

POC metrics provided by customer (from telemetry):
- Baseline steady QPS: ~120 requests/sec (mix: 60% chat gen, 30% embeddings, 10% rerank)
- Typical prompt+context size: 120 tokens in, avg 80 tokens out -> ~200 tokens per request average
- Token/sec baseline: ~24k tokens/sec sustained; peak observed: 72k tokens/sec during batch indexing windows (3x spike)
- Target latency SLOs: chat p95 < 200ms; chat p50 < 80ms; embeddings p95 < 50ms
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to commit to reserved capacity for 30-50% discount vs hosted bursts

Workshop objectives (customer wants):
- Translate QPS/token/sec into GPU counts and shapes (A10G vs H100 options). Estimate both steady-state and peak headroom.
- Verify prefix/KV caching gains on multi-turn sessions and show unit cost delta with caching on/off.
- Run live load tests against a representative model (13B quantized) to validate latency SLOs at target QPS.
- Produce a recommended reserved capacity plan (baseline + 2x burst buffer + autoscale policy) and a proposed SLA (latency targets, uptime, credit terms).

Constraints / Red flags: 
- PHI: need formal data residency controls and KMS key custody; legal flagged indemnity clauses.
- On-prem connectivity windows limited to weekends for network peering — slows validation timeline.
- SOC2 Type II report not yet shared; must be submitted before final procurement.

Quotes / customer color: 
- "We can tolerate short degradation during overnight indexing but customer-facing chat must be rock-solid during business hours." (Head of ML infra)
- "If you can give us a predictable per-token cost estimate for dedicated and a fallback strategy, procurement will move faster." (VP Product)

Recommended immediate actions (SE notes):
- Book 2-day on-site sizing workshop (day1: metrics mapping, synthetic load baseline; day2: live model runs, quantization/throughput tuning)
- Prepare a sizing worksheet mapping QPS x tokens -> GPU hrs for both 13B int8 and 7B float16. Use 90% p95 latency margin for safety.
- Draft preliminary reserved plan: baseline reserve to cover 130 QPS steady + 2x burst pool to cover 390 QPS spikes (capacity expressed as GPU equivalents; propose 8x A10G for baseline + 16x A10G burst depending on kernel results). Include cost delta vs hosted.

Notes status: customer engaged, SE onsite availability confirmed for wk of 2026-03-28, procurement timeline target May 2026.
